Likely: Great Schism (East-West, 1054), Protestant Reformation (1517-1648), and maybe the East-West Schism? Actually there are three major schisms: The Great Schism of 1054 (Eastern Orthodox vs Roman Catholic), the Protestant Reformation (splitting from Catholic Church), and the East-West Schism? Wait that's same as first. Maybe the third is the East-West Schism? Another major schism: The East-West Schism is the same as Great Schism. But maybe they refer to the "Great Schism" (1054), "Protestant Reformation" (1517-1648), and "The East-West Schism"? No.

Alternatively, the three great schisms: 1) The Great Schism of 1054 (East-West). 2) The Protestant Reformation (split into Protestant denominations). 3) The East-West Schism? Wait.

Maybe they refer to: 1) The Great Schism of 1054 (Eastern Orthodox vs Roman Catholic). 2) The Protestant Reformation (split into Protestant denominations). 3) The East-West Schism? I'm repeating.

Let's recall: There were also the "Schism of the 16th century" (Protestant Reformation). And the "Schism of the 19th century" (e.g., the Old Catholic Church after Vatican I). But the question likely expects: Great Schism (1054), Protestant Reformation (1517-1648), and the East-West Schism? Hmm.
